examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`. `onConfirm` and `onCancel` are callbacks: the modal does not close itself when you confirm, so you decide when.

examples.title: With a trigger
examples.description: Pass a `trigger` and the modal manages its own open state. Escape and Cancel close it and focus returns to the trigger.

examples.title: Destructive
examples.description: `variant="destructive"` styles the confirm action for risky changes. Pair it with `size="xs"` and a trash icon for the compact, centred layout.

examples.title: Type to confirm
examples.description: `requireText` keeps the confirm action disabled until the user types that exact phrase. The field takes focus, and the phrase clears when the modal closes.

examples.title: Form
examples.description: Pass fields as children. The first field takes focus, `confirmDisabled` blocks saving while the form is invalid, and `showCloseButton` adds the corner close button.

examples.title: With an icon
examples.description: `icon` draws a 40px tile beside the title. There is no icon unless you pass one.

examples.title: Loading
examples.description: `loading` shows a spinner on the confirm action and disables both buttons while work is in progress.

examples.title: Custom footer
examples.description: `footer` replaces the Cancel and confirm actions, for example with a single button. `footer={null}` removes the footer entirely.

examples.title: Compose the parts
examples.description: For a layout `Modal` does not cover, compose `ModalRoot`, `ModalContent`, `ModalHeader` and the rest. `ModalCancel` closes the modal; `ModalAction` does not.

examples.title: Migrating from v1
examples.description: `Dialog`, `FormModal`, `ConfirmationModal` and `DeleteConfirmationModal` are still exported from `@/components/ui/v2/modal` with their v1 props, so v1 code migrates by changing its import path.
